# A loop that stops on a declared condition

A node subscribing to its own success under a predicate iterates until the
predicate stops matching. The whole iteration is one frame. A downstream node
subscribed under the leaving predicate runs once, on the converged output.

## A self-cycle

```yaml
name: self-cycle-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: iterate
    kind: loop_counter
    cascade_mode: sequenced
    subscribes:
      - node: iterate
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count < 3"
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 50}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: downstream
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: iterate
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count >= 3"
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          count: {type: integer, default: 0}
```

The counter's `max` is 50 — far above the three rounds this cycle runs — so what
stops it is the declared predicate, not a ceiling.

## Drive it

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=1000"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/frames"
```

`iterate` emits counts 1, 2, 3 and stops. `downstream` runs exactly once, so
iteration composes with the rest of the graph. The whole iteration reads back as
a single frame in state `completed`.

## A two-node cycle

The same shape across two nodes: `pong` subscribes to `ping` under the back-edge
predicate, and `ping` subscribes back to `pong`.

```yaml
name: two-node-cycle-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: seed
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {count: {type: integer, default: 0}}}

  - type: ping
    kind: loop_counter
    subscribes:
      - node: seed
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: pong
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 50}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: pong
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ping
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count < 3"
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {count: {type: integer, default: 0}}}

  - type: downstream
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ping
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "payload.attributes_delta.count >= 3"
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {count: {type: integer, default: 0}}}
```

`ping` emits counts 1, 2, 3. `pong` runs twice — once per round below the
predicate. `downstream` runs once on the converged output. That cycle is also
one frame in state `completed`, and the instance comes to rest with no live node
runs.

A multi-node loop is an ordinary declared graph shape.
